document.title: Gromyko-Andropov-Ustinov-Ponomarev Report to CC CPSU on the Events in Afghanistan on December 27-28, 1979; December 31, 1979
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Afghanistan: Lessons from the Last War
document.note: Soviet reading of the situation in Afghanistan, presented to the Politburo on December 31 after the invasion. Source: CWIHP Bulletin 8-9, pp. 160-161.

events.description: Amin's coup and murder of Taraki.
More than 600 PDPA members, military personnel and others were executed without trial in the period following the September events.
Soviet-Afghan treaty, cited as the basis for the deployment of Soviet troops.
Armed operation by anti-Amin forces, with Soviet troops deployed, overthrew Amin's regime; Babrak Karmal's new government was formed.
New leadership released many political prisoners, including Kadyz, Keshtmand and Rafi.
Gromyko, Andropov, Ustinov and Ponomarev report No. 2519-A to the CC CPSU on events of 27-28 December.
Coup and murder of Taraki by Amin.

Soviet-Afghan treaty of 1978 cited as basis for Soviet military assistance.
Decision to send Soviet Army contingent to Afghanistan and deploy forces.

key_claims: The Soviet leadership asserts that Amin created a personal dictatorship, killed Taraki and executed more than 600 PDPA members and others after September 1979.
The report claims Amin sought a rapprochement with the United States, including secret meetings with the US chargé d'affaires in Kabul.
The report claims Amin sought compromise with Muslim fundamentalist opposition leaders through trusted intermediaries.
The authors present Soviet troop deployment as justified by the 1978 Soviet-Afghan treaty and prior requests from the earlier administration.
The report portrays Amin's overthrow as an operation by Afghan anti-Amin forces with broad popular support, with Babrak Karmal as new leader and Sarwari as deputy.
Release of political prisoners such as Kadyz, Keshtmand and Rafi is portrayed as an early step of the new government.
